title: KV cache compaction improvements — draft spec (WIP)
content:
Owner: Omar (KV cache)
Last edited by: Omar/Samir

Status: WIP draft spec. Intended to become Confluence design doc once we agree on: (1) compaction trigger + budget semantics, (2) tier-aware eviction rules, (3) safe points + correctness invariants.

TL;DR
We see tail latency spikes (p95/p99) and occasional OOM/request shedding when decode workloads run for long periods with high churn and mixed sequence lengths. Root cause appears to be KV cache allocator fragmentation + opportunistic eviction/defrag kicking in at bad times.
Proposal: add an incremental, budgeted compaction mechanism integrated with the scheduler, plus a tier-aware eviction policy for when compaction cannot reclaim contiguous space fast enough.


1) Problem statement
Today the KV cache is effectively a long-lived arena with variable-sized allocations (per sequence, per layer, per head, etc.), plus a churn pattern:
- bursts of new sequences (prefill)
- streaming decode continuing on some subset
- cancellations/timeouts at arbitrary times
- long-lived sessions (agentic / chat) coexisting with short-lived requests

Allocator currently does:
- allocate new blocks/pages for new tokens
- free blocks/pages when sequences end
- attempt best-fit-ish reuse via free lists

Failure mode we believe happens under sustained decode:
- free space exists, but is fragmented across many small holes
- new allocations require larger contiguous spans (or a specific alignment/class)
- allocator searches/defrag work increases (CPU overhead + locks)
- we hit “evict now” paths under pressure which can invalidate caches and introduce stalls
- worst case: allocation fails -> OOM handling -> shed requests / forced evictions / region-level p99 spike

Non-goals / explicitly out of scope for first iteration
- customer-facing UI for tuning knobs (Console); knobs exist as config flags only
- major kernel rewrites unrelated to KV movement (only minimal copy/pack kernels if needed)
- redesigning prefix cache semantics (but must not break them)


2) Goals and success metrics
Primary
- reduce fragmentation and make allocation time predictable under churn
- reduce p95/p99 during burst mixed-length decode workloads
- avoid OOM/shedding cases tied to fragmentation (not general capacity exhaustion)

Concrete KPIs (initial targets; verify with baseline data)
- fragmentation ratio (defined below) reduced by 2–5x in “mixed-length bursts” scenario
- decode p99 improvement: target 10–25% in synthetic and 5–15% in perf-canary
- allocation/eviction stalls: no statistically significant regression in steady-state throughput

Operational
- safe and observable: metrics + tracing + kill switch + rollback plan
- configurable by tier/model profile (Hosted default more conservative; Dedicated can trade some throughput for stability)


3) Current model (very rough) and where fragmentation comes from
This is intentionally simplified; see allocator code + Omar/Samir notes.

Memory view (arena):

|------------------------------ KV arena (GPU) ------------------------------|
| [A seq blocks] [free] [B seq blocks] [free] [C] [free] [D] [free][E] ... |

Under churn we get many small frees. Some allocations require “runs” of pages, or we may have size classes but alignment constraints still cause holes.

Observations from early measurement (staging + prod-like replay):
- fragmentation grows with mixed-length distributions (short requests die quickly leaving holes)
- fragmentation worsens when cancellations hit mid-relocation (today we don’t relocate, but cancellation timing impacts freeing patterns)
- defrag/eviction triggers coincide with p99 spikes (correlation; need causation proof)


4) Proposed approach (high level)
Add two mechanisms:
A) Compaction (new): move live KV pages to coalesce free space.
B) Eviction (formalize): if we can’t satisfy allocation within budget, evict based on policy.

Key idea: compaction is incremental and budgeted; we perform small amounts of data movement at scheduler-safe boundaries.


5) Compaction design: concepts + invariants
Terminology
- page/block: smallest alloc unit in KV arena (existing)
- segment: contiguous run of pages used as a relocation unit (new-ish concept for bookkeeping)
- relocation: copy live data from source pages to destination pages, then update mapping

Correctness invariants (must hold)
- never serve a token from “old location” after mapping update
- mapping update is atomic wrt decode kernel reading addresses
- safe point definition: relocation commit only at boundaries where no in-flight kernels reference the old pointers

Assumptions we need to validate with Noah (arch/correctness)
- we can treat prefill and decode phases as natural quiescent points for mapping updates
- scheduler can enforce a barrier for sequences involved in relocation
- we can temporarily pin a sequence (no new allocations) while relocating its tail pages


6) Where compaction runs (scheduler integration)
Option 1 (preferred): scheduler-budgeted compaction steps
- scheduler maintains a “compaction budget” (time or bytes moved) per tick/iteration
- at decode boundary (or between micro-batches), perform N relocation steps
- ensures we don’t blow p99 by doing big copies inside latency-critical segments

Option 2: background worker compaction thread
- runs independently, tries to compact opportunistically
- risk: fights with scheduler and causes bursts of GPU copy traffic at bad times
- may simplify implementation but harder to reason about tail latency

Current leaning: Option 1; use background worker only for low-priority pools or when decode queue empty.

Scheduler integration sketch (ASCII)

while (true):
  collect ready sequences
  maybe run prefill batch
  run decode microbatches
  if should_compact():
      run_compaction_step(budget)
  if memory_pressure:
      maybe_evict(budget)

Need Sofia review: choose the exact insertion point(s) so we avoid stalling decode. Candidate points:
- between prefill and decode scheduling
- after decode microbatch launch completion (host-side), before next microbatch is built
- when scheduler observes queue depth < threshold (low load)


7) Compaction trigger + stop conditions
We need a trigger to avoid constant movement.
Candidates:
- fragmentation_ratio > X for Y seconds
- allocation failure/slow path frequency > threshold
- predicted headroom < threshold for upcoming tokens

Stop conditions:
- budget exhausted
- no relocation candidates that improve contiguous free space
- risk condition: ongoing p99 increase detected (rollout guardrail)

Open question: definition of fragmentation_ratio
Proposal (simple):
- total_free_bytes / largest_free_contiguous_run_bytes
This is intuitive but can be noisy if “largest run” jumps around.
Alternative metric:
- 1 - (sum of free runs larger than size_class_min / total_free_bytes)
Needs discussion with Allison (metrics) and SRE.


8) How to compact (allocator + data movement)
Allocator changes needed (Samir)
- add an explicit representation of free runs (ordered by address)
- maintain a “frontier” pointer and a priority list of holes to fill
- track per-page ownership (sequence id, layer range, etc.) to find relocatable spans

Relocation candidate selection
- prefer moving younger pages? (lower chance of being referenced?) — probably not valid
- prefer moving pages from “high addresses” down to fill holes near low addresses
- avoid relocating sequences currently in critical decode path if it requires a barrier

Relocation steps (conceptual)
1) pick source span S and destination span D (D is a hole, size >= S)
2) issue GPU copy kernel: copy KV data from S -> D
3) at safe point, update mapping (sequence->pages) from S to D
4) mark S as free

Mapping update mechanism
- likely CPU-side pointer table update + versioning
- sequences carry a “kv_map_version”; kernels read a stable snapshot
- safe point ensures no in-flight kernel reads old version

GPU copy implementation
- minimal kernel: memcpy-like for contiguous pages, potentially batched
- for non-contiguous / strided layouts, a pack kernel may be necessary
- Hiro/Grace/Yuki: confirm if we can do it with existing primitives for initial release

Open question: do we need to compact across layers or only within a layer’s arena?
- If arenas are per-layer, compaction is independent but costs multiply
- If arena is shared, we must ensure alignment per layer/head


9) Eviction policy (tier-aware + LRU)
Motivation: compaction may be too slow under sudden bursts; eviction provides backpressure relief.

Basic rule set (WIP)
- never evict pinned sessions (Dedicated or special tiers) unless kill-switch “force” enabled
- for Hosted, allow eviction of lowest-priority sequences first
- eviction target is either:
  a) entire sequence (drop it -> request fails or is retried)
  b) prefix-cache entries (safe to regenerate)

We need a clear contract with product on customer impact. If a live sequence is evicted, what does the client see?
- error? degraded latency? fallback to smaller model? (likely outside runtime scope)

Proposed selection
- tier buckets: (pinned / normal / preemptible)
- within bucket: LRU by last_decode_timestamp
- optional: penalty for sequences with large footprint (evict big ones first under hard pressure)

Edge conditions
- streaming response in-flight: eviction must cancel request cleanly with a specific error code
- cancellation + relocation: ensure freeing is consistent (see bug found in cancelled relocation edge case)


10) Budgeting: time vs bytes moved
We need to pick a budgeting mechanism. Candidates:
- bytes_moved_per_tick: deterministic GPU copy work amount
- time_budget_ms_per_tick: dynamic based on observed copy bandwidth

Concerns
- bytes budget doesn’t cap overhead if bandwidth drops (contention)
- time budget is hard to implement reliably without GPU timing + jitter

Proposal for v1
- enforce a bytes budget, plus a hard cap on relocation steps per tick
- add a p99 guardrail: if decode p99 regresses beyond threshold for N minutes, auto-disable compaction


11) Observability / metrics (WIP list)
We need the minimum set to debug “is compaction helping or hurting?”

Allocator health
- kv_fragmentation_ratio (definition tbd)
- kv_free_bytes_total
- kv_free_run_max_bytes
- kv_alloc_slowpath_count

Compaction
- kv_compaction_bytes_moved_total
- kv_compaction_steps_total
- kv_compaction_time_ms_total (if feasible)
- kv_compaction_active_gauge (0/1)
- kv_compaction_backoff_count (budget exhausted / safe point unavailable)

Eviction
- kv_evictions_total (by reason: pressure, alloc_fail, manual)
- kv_evicted_sequences_total (by tier)
- kv_evicted_prefix_entries_total

Correlation
- tracing span per compaction step (sampled)
- exemplar linking compaction step to request latency spikes

Note: Allison wants metric naming consistent with runtime standards; Sean wants dashboards that overlay p99 and compaction bytes moved.


12) Rollout and safety
Feature flags (Benji)
- kv_compaction_enabled (default off)
- kv_compaction_budget_bytes
- kv_compaction_trigger_frag_ratio
- kv_eviction_enabled (default off initially)
- kv_eviction_tier_policy (hosted/dedicated)
- kv_compaction_kill_switch (hard disable; should stop new relocations ASAP)

Staged rollout proposal
1) internal staging + benchmark-lab: enable compaction only (no eviction)
2) perf-canary: mixed-length bursts scenario gating
3) hosted subset: 1% traffic in one region, low-risk models
4) expand hosted; then dedicated pools opt-in

Rollback
- automatic rollback if p99 increases > X% for Y minutes and compaction_active correlated
- manual kill-switch available to oncall; ensure propagation latency is acceptable

Open question: config propagation latency for kill-switch (platform team asked). Need guarantee that disable is “fast enough”. If not, runtime should also respect local “panic stop” when error budget is exceeded.


13) Test plan
Unit
- allocator invariants: free list integrity after relocation
- mapping update atomicity (mock safe point)
- eviction selection correctness (tier + LRU)

Stress/conformance (Anika)
- long-lived sessions + burst churn
- concurrent cancellations while compaction active
- partial streaming responses (client disconnect)
- adversarial: alternating huge and tiny sequences to maximize holes

Perf
- benchmark-lab new workload generator (PR-881)
- compare:
  - baseline (no compaction)
  - compaction only
  - compaction + eviction

Acceptance criteria (draft)
- no more than 1–2% throughput regression in steady-state decode
- p99 improvement in mixed-length bursts scenario OR at minimum elimination of spikes > threshold
- no correctness failures across stress suite


14) Alternatives considered (notes)
A) “Just increase KV arena size”
- helps capacity but does not solve fragmentation; also increases cost

B) “Defrag only on allocation failure”
- too late; causes worst p99 spikes because it runs in the critical path

C) “Use fixed-size blocks only; no variable allocations”
- could reduce fragmentation but increases waste; bigger change

D) “Per-sequence contiguous region reservation”
- hard with unknown decode length; would over-reserve


15) Open questions / TODOs
- [Noah] Exact safe point semantics: do we need a hard barrier for sequences being relocated? Can we guarantee no kernel reads old mapping after X?
- [Sofia] Scheduler insertion point: which phase yields least tail impact and minimal complexity?
- [Samir] Candidate selection: how to choose spans so we don’t thrash (move the same sequence repeatedly)?
- [Hiro/Grace/Yuki] Copy kernel: confirm whether existing primitives meet bandwidth needs; do we need pack/unpack for non-contiguous layouts?
- [Allison] Final metric definitions + naming + required dashboard panels
- [Sean] Rollout guardrails thresholds (p99, error rate, eviction count) + automated rollback conditions
- [Benji/Platform] Config propagation and kill-switch semantics (best-effort vs guaranteed within N seconds)
- Prefix cache interaction: what can be safely evicted without changing semantics?


16) Notes / references
- Linear epic: ENG-4821 (KV cache compaction)
- Metrics ticket: ENG-4822
- Compaction worker: ENG-4823
- Scheduler hook: ENG-4824
- Eviction policy: ENG-4825
- Kill switch + config plumbing: ENG-4826

PR sequencing (tentative)
1) PR-19342 metrics counters (land first)
2) PR-19357 allocator changes behind flag
3) PR-19371 scheduler budgeting integration
4) PR-19388 eviction policy behind separate flag
5) PR-19405 tracing spans
6) PR-19422 config plumbing + kill-switch

If you’re reading this and you’re not on runtime: this doc is not yet the source of truth. It’s the scratchpad we’ll turn into the Confluence design + ADRs once we converge on the open questions above.
